cases.derivation: From test_roster.test_reports_each_runnable_combination_as_benchmarked_or_missing. Lines run suite by suite, then each method in first-benchmarked order, then each roster model and effort in file order. claude-builtin ran only on claude-code; ce-code-review ran on claude-code (ce-retired, an off-roster model) and codex. Only twelve's luna arm runs a roster model at a roster effort; astra ran at medium. The entry without a method is skipped.

From test_one_edited_line_adds_a_model_an_effort_or_retires_a_model: one added codex model adds one missing ce-code-review line per suite after the earlier codex models, and no claude-builtin line, which never ran on codex.
From the same test: a second effort adds one line per suite after the first; twelve's astra arm ran at medium, so that line names its entry, and selected has no astra arm.
From the same test: removing astra from the roster removes exactly its lines.

From test_a_method_reaches_a_client_with_its_first_benchmark_there: one codex arm of claude-builtin, kind codex, adds claude-builtin lines for every codex roster model in every suite; only selected has the benchmark.
From test_a_benchmark_on_one_client_does_not_cover_the_model_on_another: the same model listed under codex stays missing there although its claude-code benchmark exists.

A current-cohort-input/v1 registry, the shape bench/scoreboard.current.json uses, lists each configuration once. A suite's entry takes only the configuration's sources that share a task with the suite: luna-ce is configured in first but its source covers t2 only, so first reports luna missing. ce-code-review reaches codex only through second's sources. The unplaced configuration is in no suite, so its absent arm is never read.
From test_refuses_a_roster_that_cannot_be_used. A misspelled model. Exit 1 with the violation alone on stdout; no status line is printed.
From test_refuses_a_roster_that_cannot_be_used. A client without a harness profile. Exit 1 with the violation alone on stdout; no status line is printed.
From test_refuses_a_roster_that_cannot_be_used. A client mapped to a list. Exit 1 with the violation alone on stdout; no status line is printed.
From test_refuses_a_roster_that_cannot_be_used. Efforts given as text. Exit 1 with the violation alone on stdout; no status line is printed.
From test_refuses_a_roster_that_cannot_be_used. No efforts. Exit 1 with the violation alone on stdout; no status line is printed.
From test_refuses_a_roster_that_cannot_be_used. A numeric effort. Exit 1 with the violation alone on stdout; no status line is printed.
From test_refuses_a_roster_that_cannot_be_used. A repeated effort. Exit 1 with the violation alone on stdout; no status line is printed.
From test_refuses_a_roster_that_cannot_be_used. A roster list. Exit 1 with the violation alone on stdout; no status line is printed.
From test_refuses_a_roster_that_cannot_be_used. An empty client. Exit 1 with the violation alone on stdout; no status line is printed.
Every violation is reported, client first, then each model's price and then its efforts, in roster order. A usable codex model does not suppress them.
From test_unreadable_input_exits_two: an arm kind with no client exits 2 naming the arm path and the quoted kind; stdout stays empty.
From the same test: a missing arm file exits 2 with the operating system's reason.
From the same test: a key written twice in the roster is an unreadable input, not a last-wins edit.
From the same test: malformed JSON exits 2 naming the roster. The decoder's wording after the prefix is not part of the contract.
The roster is read as UTF-8; an invalid byte exits 2 naming the roster.
From the same test: a missing roster exits 2.
An object roster needs the rate catalog to check its models; a missing catalog exits 2.
The unknown arm kind holds U+2EBF0, a CJK ideograph added in Unicode 15.1. Python 3.14's str.isprintable() accepts it, so the diagnostic's repr keeps it as written.
